title: Five Colors
label: ch:bn-five-colors
canDo: I can name five colors in Bengali and say which came from Persian, which from Sanskrit, and which is the one color where Bengali and Hindi genuinely parted ways.

payoff.summary: The chapter closes on সবুজ, 'green', a second Persian loan (sabz, the same root behind Hindi and Urdu's sabzī, 'vegetable') that sets beside লাল's own Persian gem-name. The reader names all five colors — lāl, nīl, kālo, shādā, shôbuj — and sorts them by origin: two Persian loans, two Sanskrit words, and one worn down by sound change, a more even split between inherited and borrowed than food or family showed.
